history.ask: Previous similar episodes that settled alone
Sexual history relevant to urethritis risk

red_flags: Sudden severe testicular pain, especially under 25 — torsion until proven otherwise; urgent surgical referral, do not wait for imaging
High-riding, transversely lying tender testis with absent cremasteric reflex — torsion
Scrotal or perineal skin necrosis, crepitus, or pain out of proportion in a diabetic — Fournier's gangrene; urgent surgical referral
Tender irreducible inguinoscrotal lump with vomiting — strangulated hernia; urgent surgical referral
New varicocele that is right-sided or does not empty on lying down — retroperitoneal or renal mass until excluded
exam: Compare both sides: note testicular lie and height — a high transverse testis suggests torsion
Test the cremasteric reflex on the painful side — absence supports torsion
Palpate the epididymis separately from the testis — tenderness confined to the epididymis supports epididymo-orchitis; a lump inseparable from the body of the testis is a tumor until proven otherwise
Determine whether you can get above the swelling — if not, it is inguinoscrotal (hernia)
Test for a cough impulse over the swelling
Transilluminate — brilliant transillumination supports hydrocele or epididymal cyst; a solid testis does not transilluminate
Look for the 'blue dot' of a torted appendix testis at the upper pole
Examine standing: 'bag of worms' above the testis that fills on Valsalva and empties supine — varicocele
Inspect scrotal and perineal skin for erythema, dusky patches, blisters, and crepitus
Record temperature and pulse — systemic toxicity points to epididymo-orchitis or Fournier's
Palpate the abdomen for a mass and the left renal area when a new varicocele is found

investigations.why: Pyuria and nitrites support epididymo-orchitis; a clean urine in sudden pain leans toward torsion or appendix-testis torsion
Identifies the organism behind epididymo-orchitis and separates urinary from sexually transmitted sources
Marked leukocytosis supports epididymo-orchitis or Fournier's gangrene; usually normal in torsion's first hours and in hydrocele, cyst, or varicocele
High values favor infective/inflammatory causes over torsion and over the painless swellings

Absent flow rules in torsion and increased flow rules in epididymo-orchitis — but when the story says torsion, referral must not wait for the scan; also separates cystic (hydrocele, epididymal cyst) from solid (tumor) swellings
Uncontrolled diabetes underlies Fournier's gangrene and severe epididymo-orchitis
Sent when ultrasound shows a solid testicular mass; support and stage testicular tumor before referral
